flagged.evidence: The Statement asserts contractible-fibre weak equivalences for every X and N. Take X to be a point and N=R. Imm(X,R)=R, while Imm(X×[0,1],R) has increasing and decreasing components. Restriction evaluates at 0, and each fibre has both components, so it is not contractible and the map is not a weak homotopy equivalence. Proof 1.1 incorrectly identifies that fibre with paths in Imm(X,R).

The genuine-immersion clause fails for X=[-1,1], A=[-1,-1/2]∪[1/2,1], N=R. Start with the identity and move the left component by +2t and the right by −2t. This is a path of immersions on A, but at t=1 the left interval maps to the right of the right interval. Any extension through immersions of connected X into R must remain increasing, so the path has no lift.

The Statement omits ACω, while its [L1] dependency, thm-smale-hirsch-for-open-source-manifolds, explicitly begins “Assume the axiom of countable choice”; its metric supplier thm-every-smooth-vector-bundle-admits-a-smooth-bundle-metric also explicitly assumes ACω. The statement does not make this required premise clear.

The Statement calls Immν(M,N) a subspace of Imm(M,N) consisting of immersions whose normal bundle is “identified with νF.” But def-space-of-immersions-and-space-of-formal-immersions defines Imm(M,N) as a space of maps; a chosen normal-bundle isomorphism is extra data, not represented in that subspace. If interpreted as mere isomorphism type, take M=point, N=R: the target is R, while Imm(D¹,R) has two monotonicity components, so restriction cannot be a weak homotopy equivalence.

The cited in-scope dependency lem-formal-immersion-homotopies-extend-over-a-collar concerns restrictions Imm(X×[0,1],N)→Imm(X,N) and FImm(X×[0,1],N)→FImm(X,N); it does not state a transfer from int D(νF) to D(νF). Its claimed product restriction is itself false for X=point, N=R. Thus [L2] does not license Proof 3.1’s transfer from the interior to the closed disk bundle.

The proof states “A map with contractible fibres is a weak homotopy equivalence” without establishing a fibration or a continuous fibrewise contraction. This implication is false in general: projection from the closed topologist’s sine curve onto [0,1] is surjective with contractible fibres but has two path components in its domain and one in its target.

The proof asserts that TD(νF) splits as π*TM⊕π*νF “along the horizontal and vertical directions,” but [F1] supplies only the tangent-normal splitting of (f∘π)*TN. A connection or another construction of the horizontal splitting is needed. This is a short, standard step to supply, so the gap is nonfatal.
